messages:
Sam W: Quick ask — we're onboarding PartnerCo connector in prod eu-west-1. It will egress via our NAT GW and needs outbound HTTPS to a small set of partner IPs. Can eng-security sanity-check the NAT / firewall scope and logging implications?

Sam W: Details: VPC vpc-prod-3 (10.32.0.0/16), k8s namespace partner-integrations, nat gateway nat-0abc123, nodes in private subnets. Destinations: 198.51.100.0/24 and 203.0.113.45/32.

Sam W: Proposed minimal egress SG rule: allow TCP/443 -> those two CIDRs. No inbound. Flow logs enabled to CW logs, retention 90d.

Priya K: cc @sec-reviews @Zoe L — any immediate red flags? Are we ok with exposing the NAT IPs to partner allowlist?

Miguel R: Is the partner going to log the client pod IPs or only the NAT IP? We should assume partner can see NAT IPs in allowlist.

Zoe L: From a least-privilege standpoint SG egress to those CIDRs is fine. Two things: 1) Confirm partner doesn't require IP ranges to change frequently (how will we rotate?). 2) Flow logs currently include srcaddr/dstaddr in plain text — could surface pod private IPs.

Sam W: Partner says ranges are stable for 6+ months but may add new IPs occasionally. We'll manage on their side and send updates. Rotation: we plan monthly NAT IP rotation window, but can extend.

Priya K: For the redaction: are we able to mask pod private IPs in flow logs before sending to central analytics? Our logging pipeline runs Lambda that parses / transforms CW logs. Could redact srcaddr field.

Zoe L: Yes, we can redact during ingestion. Two approval asks: 1) Approve egress-only SG to those CIDRs for namespace. 2) Approve flow-log ingestion transform that strips/masks private CIDR srcaddr fields before retention/forwarding.

Sam W: Pinging infra-bot to create the change request: 
```yaml
change: add-sg-rule
vpc: vpc-prod-3
namespace: partner-integrations
rules:
  - proto: tcp
    port: 443
    dest: ["198.51.100.0/24","203.0.113.45/32"]
    direction: egress
```

infra-bot: Change request created: CHG-2026-2417 by Sam W. Linked PR: https://git.company/repo/infra/branches/partner-egress-19851. Flow log transform flagged as dependent.

sec-reviews: Quick security note — need to ensure the transform removes any private IPs and hostnames. Approve egress rule with two conditions: (A) ingestion pipeline masks srcaddr for 10.0.0.0/8 and 172.16.0.0/12 and 192.168.0.0/16, (B) maintain audit trail of who requested allowlist additions. Also require NAT IP rotation policy documented in the ticket.

Miguel R: Will add a small Lambda step to the ingestion to replace srcaddr with "REDACTED_PRIVATE_IP" for any RFC1918 matches. Will link PR to CHG-2026-2417.

Priya K: That's acceptable. Zoe, can you sign off once the transform PR is up?

Zoe L: Yes — I'll review the transform and the SG change. If both show the masking and the rotation plan, I can sign off.

sec-reviews: Marking tentative approval in comments — final approval pending: (1) ingestion transform PR, (2) NAT rotation schedule in CHG-2026-2417, (3) post-deploy verification steps added to runbook.

Sam W: Thanks — I'll open the transform ticket and update the change with rotation schedule. Will ping when PRs are ready. :thumbsup:

Priya K: Thanks Sam. Leaving this thread open until Zoe thumbs up.

Sam W: update 45m later — transform PR opened: https://git.company/repo/logs/transform/PR-512, includes unit tests for masking. CHG updated with rotation: monthly, documented owner: infra-nat-team.

Zoe L: Reviewing PR now. Small nit: please ensure logs still capture destination IP for debugging (don't redact dstaddr for external CIDRs). Otherwise LGTM.

sec-reviews: Final approval granted. Conditions verified: masking in ingestion, NAT rotation added, runbook steps present. Closing with ticket link: SEC-482.

Sam W: deploying change this afternoon per maintenance window. Will post verification results here after deploy.

Miguel R: Post-deploy verification: confirmed outbound to 198.51.100.23:443 from podX reached partner and flow log entry shows dstaddr=198.51.100.23 but srcaddr=REDACTED_PRIVATE_IP. All good.

Sam W: closing thread — thanks everyone! :party:
